# Review contracts, lenses, and lifecycle mapping

<!-- Generated by generate_agent_definitions.py; do not edit. -->
<!-- delivery-version: 96a1e289289a180161258baa10f7547b8cd9f719 2026-11-07T11:55:51+01:00 -->

Lenses registered by `aiscr-review-pr`.

| Lens | Contract | Focus | Exclusions | Cost | Availability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| survey | survey | Complete read of the assigned material producing its inventory, receipts, and lens-relevant signals. | Defect adjudication, severity assignment, and proposed fixes. | standard | survey |
| correctness | findings | State, data integrity, concurrency, types, and resource lifetime. | Security exploitation, performance-only costs, and interface/documentation contracts. | standard | default |
| security | findings | Authorization, input trust, injection, secrets, cryptography, and exposure. | Style, unsupported hypothetical exploits, and operational defects with no trust-boundary consequence. | deep | default |
| integration | findings | API, documentation, dependency, build, test, frontend, CI/CD, and operational contracts. | Internal state defects, performance-only costs, security exploitation, and claims of live behavior without probe evidence. | standard | default |
| performance | findings | Queries, repeated work, blocking I/O, memory, startup, and build/runtime resource cost. | Speculative micro-optimizations without a reachable workload or consequential cost. | standard | default |
| duplication | findings | Repeated authored behavior or facts that produce inconsistent fixes and maintenance. | Generated mirrors, deliberate specializations, and similar text with different obligations. | economy | default |
| dead-code | findings | Unreachable first-party behavior, unused configuration, and obsolete integration paths. | Compiler/linter findings, dynamic entry points whose reachability is unresolved, and vendored internals. | economy | default |
| deploy-safety | findings | Migration ordering, rollback, release compatibility, startup sequencing, and recovery. | Security exploitation and generic build failures already owned by integration. | deep | target-enabled |
| verify | verification | Focused verification of candidate findings and prior-finding dispositions. | Fresh broad review and replacement findings outside the assigned candidates. | economy | verification |

<!-- aiscr:ecosystem-only -->

| Family | Kind | Lens mapping | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T01 | lifecycle | none | Repository inventory establishes material and boundaries for every later phase; it is not a defect dimension. |
| T02 | analysis | integration, correctness, security, duplication, dead-code | Dependency compatibility, cycles, supply-chain trust, and authored architectural overlap cross several concerns. |
| T03 | analysis | correctness, performance, security, deploy-safety | Data integrity, query cost, access boundaries, and optional migration safety retain separate judgments. |
| T04 | analysis | integration, security, performance, deploy-safety | Build/container contracts, exposure, resource cost, and optional rollout recovery remain covered. |
| T05 | analysis | security | The security phase supplies production and supply-chain evidence to the security dimension. |
| T06 | analysis | correctness, performance, integration | Async state, idempotence, blocking calls, routing, and external-service contracts remain covered. |
| T07 | analysis | correctness, security, integration, performance, duplication, dead-code | First-party frontend behavior crosses all default dimensions, including integrity and public contracts. |
| T08 | analysis | integration, duplication, correctness | Documentation/code agreement, authored duplication, and generator failures retain their checks. |
| T09 | analysis | integration, security, performance, deploy-safety | CI/CD, testing and supply-chain controls, caching, and optional release safety remain covered. |
| T10 | analysis | integration, correctness, security, duplication, dead-code | Operational contracts, failure behavior, destructive inputs, overlap, and obsolete paths remain covered. |
| T11 | lifecycle | none | Final synthesis and mechanical integrity checks consume completed phase evidence; they are not another review dimension. |
| T12 | external-workflow | integration, performance, security | Deployed UI/SEO retains aiscr-review-prod-ui acquisition and output; these dimensions interpret its probe evidence, never replace live probing with static review. |
| T13 | external-workflow | integration | API spec/doc agreement retains aiscr-review-api-doc and its target-owned applicability. |
| live-acceptance | external-workflow | correctness, integration, security | Issue-driven acceptance and regressions retain aiscr-review-live discovery, in-session probes, and corpus reporting. |
